objective: Al terminar cuentas una historia o anécdota con tiempos narrativos (pasado simple, continuo, perfecto y perfecto continuo), conectores de secuencia y recursos para crear tensión.

warmup.prompt_es: Contar bien una historia exige elegir el tiempo verbal correcto para el fondo y la acción, y dosificar la información. Practicas la estructura narrativa y los recursos de suspense.

text: It was a Friday evening, and I had been working since six in the morning. I was exhausted, so when the train pulled into the station, I jumped on without checking the destination board. I sat down, closed my eyes and fell asleep almost immediately.

When I woke up, the carriage was empty and it was dark outside. I had no idea where I was. A conductor was walking along the platform, so I ran out and asked him. 'This is the last stop,' he said. 'The train has been going north for two hours.'

I couldn't believe it. I had boarded the wrong train! My phone had run out of battery, and the next train home wasn't until the following morning. Fortunately, a kind woman who had been waiting for her husband offered me a lift to a small hotel nearby.

As soon as I walked in, I realised that I had left my bag on the train. At that moment, I almost burst into tears. Suddenly, the receptionist smiled and held up my bag. 'The conductor brought it here,' she explained. I have never been so relieved in my life.
The next morning, I caught the right train. Since then, I always check the board twice.
input.es: El tren equivocado. Era un viernes por la tarde y yo llevaba trabajando desde las seis de la mañana. Estaba agotado, así que cuando el tren entró en la estación, subí sin mirar el panel de destino. Me senté, cerré los ojos y me dormí casi enseguida. Cuando me desperté, el vagón estaba vacío y fuera era de noche. No tenía idea de dónde estaba. Un revisor caminaba por el andén, así que salí corriendo y le pregunté. 'Esta es la última parada', dijo. 'El tren lleva dos horas yendo hacia el norte.' No podía creerlo. ¡Había subido al tren equivocado! Mi móvil se había quedado sin batería y el siguiente tren a casa no salía hasta la mañana siguiente. Afortunadamente, una mujer amable que estaba esperando a su marido me ofreció llevarme a un pequeño hotel cercano. En cuanto entré, me di cuenta de que había dejado mi bolso en el tren. En ese momento casi me eché a llorar. De pronto, la recepcionista sonrió y levantó mi bolso. 'El revisor lo trajo aquí', explicó. Nunca me había sentido tan aliviado en mi vida. A la mañana siguiente cogí el tren correcto. Desde entonces, siempre compruebo el panel dos veces.

md_es: **Tiempos narrativos**
| Tiempo | Uso en la historia | Ejemplo |
| **Past simple** | acciones principales, en orden | *I jumped on the train and fell asleep.* |
| **Past continuous** | fondo, escena, acción en curso | *It was getting dark. A conductor was walking along the platform.* |
| **Past perfect** | lo que ocurrió antes | *I had boarded the wrong train.* |
| **Past perfect continuous** | duración antes de otro momento | *I had been working since six.* |
| **Used to / would** | hábitos pasados | *I used to take that train every day.* |
**Estructura de una buena anécdota**
1. **Escena inicial** (cuándo, dónde, quién): *It was a Friday evening…*
2. **Problema o giro:** *When I woke up, the carriage was empty.*
3. **Complicación:** *My phone had run out of battery.*
4. **Clímax:** *Suddenly, the receptionist held up my bag.*
5. **Resolución y reflexión:** *Since then, I always check the board twice.*
**Conectores de secuencia**
- Inicio: *At first, To begin with, It all began when…*
- Desarrollo: *Then, After that, Meanwhile, Later, As soon as, While, By the time…*
- Giro: *Suddenly, All of a sudden, Out of nowhere, To my surprise…*
- Final: *In the end, Eventually, Finally, Looking back…*
**Crear suspense**
- Frases cortas en el momento de tensión: *Silence. Then a noise.*
- Preguntas retóricas: *What could it be?*
- Adverbios: *nervously, suddenly, fortunately, unfortunately.*
**Estilo directo**
- *'This is the last stop,' he said.* · *'What are you doing here?' she asked.*
- Variar los verbos: *whisper, shout, murmur, reply, explain, mutter.*
**Errores típicos**
- ✘ *When I arrived, the train already left.* → ✔ *When I arrived, the train had already left.*
- ✘ *I was walk home when it started to rain.* → ✔ *I was walking home when it started to rain.*
- ✘ *I have lost my bag yesterday.* → ✔ *I lost my bag yesterday.* (no present perfect con *yesterday*)
- ✘ *While I slept, the phone rang* (acción larga interrumpida) → ✔ *While I was sleeping, the phone rang.*
- ✘ *In the end of the story…* → ✔ *At the end of the story… / In the end, …*
**Ojo:** *At the end* (final concreto) ≠ *In the end* (finalmente). *Suddenly* y *eventually* son sudden/eventual con sentido distinto: *eventually* = finalmente, no 'eventualmente'.
Pronunciación: *carriage* /ˈkærɪdʒ/ · *conductor* /kənˈdʌktə/ · *relieved* /rɪˈliːvd/ · *eventually* /ɪˈventʃuəli/.
